ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening against HM Treasury UK Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Sanctions Lists, Gibraltar FSC Sanctions Notices and Cayman Islands CIMA watchlists, plus a 24-hour adverse-media and PEP check. Screening applies to all UBOs at or above 25%, directors, signatories and high-risk commercial counterparties. Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory for PEPs, FATF grey-list jurisdictions, cross-border logistics counterparties and cash-intensive settlement, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation. A compliance memorandum recording screening results must be placed in the corporate file before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (CSRA) e-filing portal and Cayman Islands General Registry via CIMA Online Filing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be rendered in the Latin alphabet (A-Z). No Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic or other scripts are accepted in the official corporate record. The name of the Gibraltar foreign company must replicate the exact Roman-script name of the Cayman Exempted Company, with the statutory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' as required by the Cayman certificate. Non-Latin trade names may be used for branding but cannot appear in the registry record. Punctuation and special characters are confined to hyphens, ampersands and common corporate markers; diacritical marks are discouraged and automatically machine-stripped in the Gibraltar registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected by the Gibraltar Companies Registry, the applicant must file a Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, accompanied by a statutory declaration and, if the rejection concerns a sensitive token, a prior Ministerial Consent from the Government of Gibraltar. If the reconsideration is dismissed, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Financial Services and Pensions Ombudsman, and further judicial review may be sought at the Gibraltar Supreme Court within 30 days. A rejected Cayman name may be challenged by judicial review before the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands within 30 days. A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing a renewal application and paying the prescribed fee before expiry; reservations are non-transferable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office in either Cayman or Gibraltar. The Cayman Exempted Company must maintain a physical registered office at a CIMA-licensed corporate services provider in George Town, Grand Cayman. The Gibraltar branch must maintain a physical registered office address in Gibraltar, not a P.O. box, for service of process and statutory records. Virtual correspondence and mailbox services may be used for ancillary customer-facing functions only, but the economic substance assessment for a cross-dock/3PL operator requires a physical operational presence (warehouse or contractual warehousing capacity) in sufficient form to evidence active conduct of the logistics business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-High for Gibraltar: 70% probability of an unannounced inspection by Gibraltar Customs, the Gibraltar Income Tax Office, and the GFIU within the first 18 months of registration to verify economic substance, excise and customs compliance. Low for Cayman registered agent premises: approximately 10% annual probability of a CIMA desktop or physical audit cycle review. Inspections may be triggered by incomplete substance documentation or adverse sanctions alerts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), ss. 14, 16, 21, 23, 34 and 54 (exempted company formation); Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, ss. 30-36 and ss. 437-450 (registration as an overseas company with a place of business in Gibraltar); Gibraltar Companies (Fees) Regulations; Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Corporate Affairs; Gibraltar Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (Cayman Islands Exempted Company); Overseas Company Registration Statement (Form OS1) filed with the Gibraltar Companies Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Cayman exempted company; authorised share capital of US$50,000 (or 50,000 shares) must be stated in the Memorandum of Association. No escrow or deposit requirement. Gibraltar branch registration imposes no capital requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first board meeting, that: (1) the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, as executed, are adopted; (2) the subscriber's subscription for one Ordinary Share is accepted, and that share is allotted and issued at par value nil premium; (3) the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Cayman registered office address], and an overseas establishment/branch is registered in Gibraltar at [Gibraltar registered address]; (4) [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed as initial directors, [Secretary] as company secretary, and [Officer] as money laundering compliance officer; (5) each officer is authorised individually to execute, file, and effect registration with the Cayman Islands General Registry and Gibraltar Companies Registry, and to fulfil all statutory filing obligations; (6) share certificates and corporate registers be immediately issued and opened.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and corporate personality pre-filing review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Corporate Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name for availability check against the Cayman Islands Companies Registry and, conditionally, against the Gibraltar Companies Registry name list. If the name is unavailable, provide two alternate names. Once acceptable, lock the name for use in the constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two alternate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit alternate names within two business days; where the Registrar has issued a formal refusal, a judicial review application may be made within the prescribed period or an amended name may be re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarisation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office Provider / Notary Public in the Cayman Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in exempted company form, including the exempted company objects clause, share capital clause, and standard regulatory language. Execute the subscriber signature pages before a notary public and arrange the Declaration of Compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries wording, file conformed exhibits or a supplementary statutory declaration within five business days, or submit a revised draft for expedited re-review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cayman incorporation filing and government fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Corporate Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed constitutional documents, Declaration of Compliance, and the applicable government filing fee through a licensed registered office provider. Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation upon satisfactory review by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Form of Registration / Declaration of Compliance
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defective declaration and file amended constitutional documents; pay the applicable late fee or expedited fee if resubmission is necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution and opening of corporate registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Registered Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution in lieu. Approve the allotment and issue of the subscriber share, adopt the corporate seal and share certificate template, appoint directors and the secretary, and open the register of members, register of directors, and register of charges.
required_dossiers: Notice of meeting or written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any omission in the statutory registers and file a late event return where required; if the written resolution is defective, execute a confirmatory resolution and attach it to the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after establishing a place of business in Gibraltar, file the certified Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, certified Memorandum and Articles, list of directors and secretary, particulars of the Gibraltar registered office address, and the statement of compliance for an overseas company. Pay the prescribed filing fee and obtain the Gibraltar overseas company number.
required_dossiers: Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association
Gibraltar registered office consent and address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries certified translations, registered office consent, or the list of directors, submit corrected documents within ten business days; apply for late filing relief if the initial deadline has passed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar corporate tax, employment, and AML registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office / Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the overseas establishment for Gibraltar Income Tax purposes using the standard non-resident company registration form. If the branch employs staff, register for PAYE and social insurance. Appoint a designated officer for AML compliance under the Proceeds of Crime Act and, where a relevant activity is carried out, make an application to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission for AML supervision.
required_dossiers: Payroll and PAYE registration details (if applicable)
AML compliance policy and designated officer appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond promptly to HM Government of Gibraltar queries by providing the corrected documentation; if the AML classification is disputed, request a determination review from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licensing Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Department of Enterprise and Employment)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gibraltar Trade Licence / Warehouse and Distribution Facility Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Sustainability, Climate Change and Heritage (DESCCH), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Screening and Registration (low-impact cross-dock logistics); full Environmental Impact Statement will be required only if the site exceeds one hectare or is located within a protected/prescribed sensitive area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewer: pH 6-10, suspended solids <=300 mg/L, BOD5 <=250 mg/L, oils and grease <=50 mg/L; air emissions must meet Gibraltar/UK Clean Air standards with a workplace VOC concentration limit of 50 mg/m3; hazardous waste storage and consignment must comply with the Gibraltar Waste Management Regulations and the European Waste Catalogue; all waste shipment records must be retained for five years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service covering warehouse racking, emergency lighting, extinguishers, sprinklers, and evacuation routes; structural load inspection certificate from Building Control under the Gibraltar Building Act; occupational health and safety clearance from the Gibraltar Health and Safety Authority for forklift areas, manual handling, battery charging, and racking integrity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Department of Tax and Customs (HM Customs Gibraltar and the Income Tax Office); online portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/ and https://www.egov.gi/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Cayman exempted company is not categorised as a tax resident absent a local permanent establishment, local management or Gibraltarian source income. A foreign entity wishing to open a branch or establish a taxable presence in Gibraltar must register with the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014 and obtain an Income Tax reference number from the Income Tax Office; the application includes certified constitutional documents, director/officer details, registered office address, beneficial ownership information and a branch return filing. No VAT identification number is applicable because Gibraltar sits outside the EU VAT area and levies no VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate an OECD-style check-the-box election. The Income Tax Act 2010 applies territorial taxation, generally charging income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar. Certain structured finance or international holding entities may apply for exempt or qualifying category treatment, but a Cayman exempted company performing overseas fulfilment services will have no Gibraltar-source income and no filing obligation absent a permanent establishment. Hybrid mismatch rules under BEPS Action 2 are domestically limited and do not create standalone election mechanisms for exempted foreign companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax regime exists in Gibraltar; indirect taxation is limited to import duty, excise duty, and stamp duty on specific instruments.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no local VAT/GST registration threshold applies. Import duty is payable at the time of importation into Gibraltar and is collected by HM Customs regardless of turnover; no separate tax registration is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar has no mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API acceptance or digital stamping obligation for commercial sales or services. Customs declarations are transmitted electronically through the Gibraltar Customs electronic platform, but no continuous transaction controls or cryptographic clearance mandates apply to business-to-business or business-to-consumer invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – Gibraltar does not operate a VAT/GST system, so there is no 0% export tax rate to claim and no indirect tax refund mechanism. Exports of physical goods from Gibraltar to non-EU destinations are not subject to local import or export duties; cross-border services supplied by the Cayman entity to overseas customers fall outside the territorial scope of Gibraltar income tax and are subject to no indirect tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (electronic Single Administrative Document equivalent)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill as transport evidence
Proof of exit from Gibraltar territory (customs electronic confirmation or port authority clearance)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT zero-rating clawback exists because the jurisdiction has no VAT. Penalties may arise under the Customs and Excise Act and Gibraltar customs law for false export declarations, unauthorised removal of goods or failure to produce required documents; applicable sanctions include forfeiture of goods, monetary penalties up to three times the evaded duty, civil penalties and, for fraudulent acts, criminal prosecution before the Gibraltar courts. HM Customs may retrospectively review prior declarations and adjust customs liabilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No indigenous central bank. The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the statutory banking regulator under the Financial Services Act 2019 (FSA 2019) and exercises AML/CTF supervision. Monetary authority is structurally delegated to the Bank of England / HM Treasury: the Government of Gibraltar issues the Gibraltar pound (GIP) exclusively under the Currency Notes Act 1934 with 100% Bank of England sterling backing at a fixed 1:1 peg, operating a currency-board model. The GFSC has no reserve-management or lender-of-last-resort powers; it prunes conduct and prudential regulation only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unconditional convertibility across both current and capital accounts. GIP is exchangeable at par into Bank of England notes for residents and non-residents, with no approval thresholds, no repatriation licensing and no remaining restrictions of the repealed UK Exchange Control Act 1947 (extended to Gibraltar and repealed in 1979). Dividends, intercompany loan repayments, trademark royalties and capital repatriation from the Cayman Exempted Company's Gibraltar treasury to its Cayman parent are unrestricted in GIP, GBP, EUR and USD. The only practical frictions are AML/CTF high-risk screening under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, and financial-sanctions vetting under the Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020 (consolidated). For an e-commerce fulfilment treasury, a GBP/GIP liquidity buffer should be retained to avoid spread drag when converting EUR and USD settlement receivables.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multicurrency account (GIP/GBP/EUR/USD) with optional merchant-settlement escrow sub-account
Operational current account (GIP/GBP/EUR) for trade-related flows
Operational account plus documentary trade finance (Letters of Credit, collections)
Operational account with SME lending and treasury services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Santander Totta S.A. - Gibraltar Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EUR-denominated operational account using Iberian clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for treasury disbursement rails, but with a structural caution: Gibraltar has no active indigenous EMI licence market of scale, so the Cayman entity should contract with UK FCA-authorised EMIs or EEA-passported EMIs — Airwallex (UK) Limited, Wise Platform and Revolut Business are the leading candidates matching the target rails (Local_ACH, Airwallex, Wire). Legal constraints: (1) FCA EMIs are not Gibraltar deposit-takers; balances are safeguarded, not covered by the Gibraltar Statutory Deposit Guarantee Scheme of up to GIP 100,000 per depositor, so a GFSC-licensed bank must remain the settlement anchor and primary repository of capital; (2) the EMI account agreement must permit non-UK corporate ownership (Cayman exempted companies are generally accepted by Airwallex and Wise, subject to enhanced due diligence); (3) no borrowing, overdraft or escrow functions may reside at the EMI if the 3PL master agreements require segregated client funds, making a commercial bank (NatWest/Trusted Novus) indispensable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: GFSC rules technically permit remote/video KYC, but Gibraltar commercial banks uniformly impose a physical interview for offshore-incorporated vehicles such as a Cayman Exempted Company: at least one director (or the appointed GFSC-licensed Corporate Services Provider principal) must attend in person at onboarding at NatWest Gibraltar and Gibraltar International Bank; Trusted Novus and APS may accept a notarised appointment of a Gibraltar CSP coupled with a video call. Recommended practical route: appoint a GFSC-licensed CSP (e.g., Sovereign Trust or Hassans) as registered agent and signatory co-ordinator; the CSP principal attends the bank meeting, satisfying the physical-presence condition without board travel. Thereafter, fully remote e-banking is operationally normal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore shell typology: Cayman Exempted Company with Tax_Exempt_Zone classification, zero minimum capital, non-resident ownership permitted; bank policy flags 0% corporate tax jurisdictions and screens 'Cayman tax-exempt' as a high-risk marker.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Apostilled Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and certified Register of Directors and Members; (2) Cayman Islands International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Law (2020 Revision) annual filing evidencing that core 3PL income-generating activities are performed in Gibraltar/UK, or the pure-equity-holding exemption; (3) Confirmation of non-Cayman tax residency and, if applicable, Gibraltar Income Tax Office certificate; (4) Bank reference letter from a prime Cayman or UK bank covering 24 months of transactional history; (5) FBI/PEP and sanctions screens on all UBOs with source-of-wealth statements; (6) Board resolution designating the Gibraltar CSP as agent for service and AML liaison.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingled marketplace receivables: Amazon, eBay and Shopify settlements arriving via omnibus payment references to a single IBAN, triggering transaction-laundering and unlicensed-money-services typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed master 3PL fulfilment agreements with each marketplace merchant; (2) Marketplace seller-central dashboard extracts for the prior 12 months reconciled to bank credits; (3) A2X or equivalent reconciliation ledger mapping monthly settlement summaries to invoice-level line items; (4) Customs evidence of physical movement — EORI/GB number, C88 customs declarations and CDS import/export records authorising cross-dock flows through Gibraltar; (5) Standard operating cash-flow model demonstrating whether the entity is a disclosed agent or riskless principal, capping the AML suspicion window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Management opacity: Cayman shareholders/directors with no physical footprint in Gibraltar or the UK, failing the bank's substance test for a tax-exempt offshore vehicle; FATF grey-list historical memory of Cayman (removed 27 October 2023).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) KYC/UBO pack for each director and 25%+ shareholder: passport, proof of residential address, professional CV and sworn source-of-wealth/source-of-funds forms; (2) Gibraltar lease agreement for the cross-dock warehouse, utility bills and payroll records for on-island staff; (3) IRIS/CRS/FATCA registration confirming tax-transparency filing in both Cayman and Gibraltar; (4) Statutory PSC registers certified to be current; (5) Written FATF status note appended to the bank's jurisdiction assessment confirming the Cayman Islands are no longer under increased monitoring; (6) If requested, chartered accountant's independent working-capital and funding-structure opinion to evidence genuine commercial purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Step 1 - Cayman side: shareholder capital contribution authorised by Cayman board resolution (no minimum capital regime and no CIMA approval), remitted via a SWIFT member bank in the Cayman Islands (e.g., Butterfield Bank). Step 2 - Rail selection: USD injection uses MT103 routed via NatWest Gibraltar's US correspondent (Fedwire) with 2-3 business day value; GBP uses CHAPS same-day into the bank's UK settlement account; EUR uses TARGET2 via Santander Totta/commercial correspondent because Gibraltar has no direct T2 membership. Step 3 - Payment message discipline: MT103 Field 70 (Remittance Information) must quote 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CAYMAN EXEMPTED CO - BOARD RESOLUTION [DATE]', Field 72 '/REC/' account-name, and the settlement-purpose narrative classified as 'Equity injection, non-trade' for BoE/GFSC statistical reporting; MT202 COV accompanies the cover payment for USD. Step 4 - Verification and use: post-credit, the bank requires the signed source-of-funds attestation and CRS/FATCA IGA filings to be triggered in both Gibraltar and Cayman; funds cannot fund trade payables until the compliance clearance is returned.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Rails by class: (1) International supplier payments (goods procurement, line-haul, last-mile carriers): SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 quoting invoice numbers and unique SPOT transaction code for GL reconciliation; (2) UK and EU supplier settlements for warehouse consumables: Faster Payments/SEPA via Airwallex GBP/EUR e-wallet as the primary Local_ACH rail; (3) Large-volume consignments and customs bonds in excess of £50,000: Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by NatWest Gibraltar or Trusted Novus Bank, with presentation pack comprising commercial invoice, B/L or AWB, packing list and warehouse receipt; (4) Payroll, rent and port charges: local ACH/Faster Payments and CHAPS for HMRC CDS customs payments using HMRC's specific GB/EORI payment reference; (5) Surplus repatriation to the Cayman parent: MT103 with purpose 'dividend' or 'intercompany loan repayment' supported by Cayman board minutes and, where relevant, a Gibraltar Statement of Testimony on withholding status, transmitted via the same correspondent chain used for inbound to evidence closed-loop traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (GIP/GBP versus EUR and USD; tenors 1M-12M) with GFSC-licensed banks (NatWest Gibraltar, Trusted Novus) under ISDA 2002, collaterised to EMIR NFC- clearing thresholds.

Cash-settled Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on EUR/USD and USD/GBP for tenors where physical delivery of GIP is operationally inefficient; permitted for a non-financial counterparty treasury only with top-20 global bank counterparties.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/GBP and USD/GBP) to convert EUR-dominated marketplace receivables into the GIP/GBP liability currency for customs, payroll and landlord obligations under IFRS 9 fair-value hedge accounting.

Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (EUR/GBP, USD/GBP) covering Q4 peak-season settlement volatility; premiums expensed to treasury cost within the 3PL cost base; naked speculative positioning prohibited.

Forward overlay via the Airwallex or Wise FX desk for sub-£50,000 monthly flows where bank-line headroom is better deployed on documentary trade limits; such instruments must be booked under the EMI's FCA permissions and remain below the EMIR clearing threshold.

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (Gibraltar permanent establishment trading profits); 0% statutory Cayman corporate tax for the Cayman Exempted Company
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar: territorial taxation for non-residents (only PE-attributable profits taxed); no capital gains tax; no VAT; no dividend withholding tax; Cayman Exempted Company tax exemption undertaking (normally 20 years, renewable); Gibraltar participation exemption may apply to dividends from qualifying substantial shareholdings
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite for Gibraltar trading losses (no statutory cap; carry-back unavailable; continuity-of-trade conditions may apply)
